article.title: Why a Successful A/B Test May Fail When Rolled Out to Everyone
article.why: Understand why experimental effects may change at full scale.

paragraphs.en:
A successful A/B test is encouraging, but it does not guarantee that a campaign will produce the same result when rolled out to the entire customer base. Experiments estimate an effect under specific conditions. Full deployment can change those conditions.

The first issue is population mix. An experiment may include only customers who are eligible for a message, reachable through a certain channel, or active during a particular period. If the rollout later includes broader or different groups, the average treatment effect can change because those customers may respond differently.

The second issue is capacity. A small test may create a few thousand inquiries that a call center can handle easily. A national rollout may create hundreds of thousands. Waiting times can rise, service quality can fall, and the customer experience can deteriorate. The treatment itself has not changed, but the system around it has.

Channel saturation is another risk. During a test, customers may receive one distinctive message. During full deployment, the same channel may carry many campaigns at once. More messages can reduce attention, increase opt-outs, or make offers compete with one another. A response rate observed in a clean test environment may therefore be too optimistic.

There can also be interference between customers. A promotion tested on a small group may have little effect on inventory or social behavior. At scale, however, products may sell out, prices may change, or customers may share information with untreated people. Standard A/B analysis often assumes that one customer’s treatment does not affect another customer’s outcome, but large-scale deployment can weaken that assumption.

For these reasons, teams should treat rollout as another measurement stage rather than the end of measurement. Before scaling, check whether the target population, channel, operational capacity, and offer remain comparable with the experiment. Consider a staged rollout, such as 10 percent, 30 percent, and then 100 percent, while monitoring conversion, complaints, opt-outs, cost, and service metrics.

A good experiment answers, ‘Did this treatment work under the tested conditions?’ A rollout decision asks a broader question: ‘Will it still create net value at this scale, for this population, with these operational constraints?’ Keeping these questions separate helps organizations avoid turning a statistically successful test into an operational failure.
paragraphs.zh:
成功的 A/B test 很令人鼓舞，但不保證擴大到全體顧客後仍有相同效果。實驗是在特定條件下估計效果，而全面 rollout 本身可能改變這些條件。

第一是 population mix。實驗可能只包含符合配信資格、可由特定渠道接觸、或特定期間活躍的顧客；若正式展開時母體更廣或不同，平均 treatment effect 可能改變。

第二是 capacity。小規模測試帶來幾千件詢問時客服中心能處理，但全國 rollout 可能帶來數十萬件，等待時間上升、服務品質下降，顧客體驗惡化。Treatment 沒變，周邊系統卻變了。

Channel saturation 也是風險。測試時顧客只看到一則醒目的訊息，全面展開時同一渠道可能同時承載多個 campaign，注意力下降、退訂增加、offer 彼此競爭，因此測試環境的 response rate 可能過度樂觀。

顧客間還可能存在 interference。小群體促銷對庫存或社交行為影響有限，但大規模後可能缺貨、價格改變、顧客互相分享資訊，使「一人的 treatment 不影響另一人的 outcome」這項標準假設變弱。

因此 rollout 應被視為下一個 measurement stage。擴大前確認 target population、channel、operational capacity 與 offer 是否仍與實驗相近，並考慮 10%、30%、100% 的 staged rollout，同時監控 conversion、complaint、opt-out、cost 與 service metrics。

實驗回答的是「在測試條件下有效嗎？」Rollout 決策則是「在這個規模、母體與營運限制下仍能創造淨價值嗎？」分開這兩個問題，能避免統計成功卻營運失敗。
paragraphs.ja:
成功したA/B testでも、全顧客へrolloutしたとき同じ効果が出るとは限りません。実験は特定条件下のeffectを推定しますが、全面展開はその条件自体を変える可能性があります。

第一はpopulation mixです。実験対象が配信資格者、特定channelで到達可能な人、特定期間のactive顧客に限定されている場合、rolloutで対象を広げると平均treatment effectが変わり得ます。

第二はcapacityです。小規模testの数千件の問い合わせならcall centerで処理できても、全国展開で数十万件になれば待ち時間やservice qualityが悪化します。treatmentは同じでも周辺systemが変わります。

channel saturationもあります。testでは一つのmessageが目立っても、全面展開時に複数campaignが同じchannelを使えば、attention低下、opt-out増加、offer同士の競合が起こります。

顧客間のinterferenceも無視できません。小規模ではinventoryへの影響がなくても、scaleすると品切れや価格変化、情報共有が生じます。一人へのtreatmentが他人のoutcomeに影響しないという標準的な仮定が弱まります。

そのためrolloutもmeasurement stageとして扱います。target population、channel、運用capacity、offerが実験時と比較可能か確認し、10％、30％、100％の段階展開を行いながらconversion、苦情、opt-out、cost、service指標を監視します。

実験は「tested conditionsで効いたか」を答え、rolloutは「この規模・母集団・運用制約でもnet valueを生むか」を問います。両者を分けることが、統計的成功を運用上の失敗に変えないために重要です。

vocabulary.usage: Customer interference can appear at scale.

business.term: Rollout is another measurement stage, not the end of measurement.
business.explanation: 強調正式展開仍需持續測量。
